title: Launch Brief (Draft) — Hosted Data Residency Enforcement (Region Pinning) — Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation
content:
Launch Brief (Draft v0.3)
Hosted Data Residency Enforcement ("Region Pinning")
Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation

Owner: Avery Johnson (Enterprise rollout coordination)
EMEA owner: Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineering lead: Markus Klein
Product owner: Naomi Feldman
Security Eng: Marcus Lin | Exec sponsor: Dr. Aisha Rahman
SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
Docs: Elliot Price (lead), Wei Chen, Kira Thompson
Last updated: 2025-02-28

1) TL;DR
We are launching customer-configurable region pinning + deterministic request-time enforcement for the Redwood Hosted API. Enterprise customers can declare an allowed region set (e.g., EU-only) and a primary region. Requests that would violate residency are blocked with consistent HTTP status + machine-readable error codes and guidance. Goal: unblock regulated prospects (payments/health/regulated SaaS) and reduce security review friction while ensuring we do not route/fallback/log content outside the pinned region(s).

2) What is launching
Feature name (external): Data Residency Enforcement (Hosted) / Region Pinning
Internal name: Hosted data residency enforcement

Core capabilities (MVP / GA target):
- Control plane configuration: org/project (and optional API key) residency policy
  - Allowed regions: set of regions where customer content may be processed
  - Primary region: preferred region for routing when multiple allowed
- Enforcement at request time:
  - Routing layer respects allowed regions
  - Cross-region fallback is disabled by default when policy is present
  - Clear, consistent error response when a request cannot be served within the allowed region(s)
- Observability + auditability:
  - Residency decision context logged for debugging (without leaking content)
  - Dashboards for blocked requests + policy evaluation latency
  - Audit log events for policy create/update/delete and any admin override
- Console UX:
  - Residency settings page (set primary + allowed regions)
  - Configuration change history
  - Blocked request troubleshooting view (recent blocks, reasons, request_id)

Explicit limitations to message (important for security reviews):
- Not “multi-region replication” of customer data
- Does not automatically geo-fence every internal subsystem on day one; initial scope is routing/gateway/logging boundaries with phased hardening follow-ups
- Dedicated and Private: Dedicated aligns where applicable (routing/fallback constraints), but contractual/data-plane differences apply; Private is customer-controlled by design

3) Why now (customer pull + competitive pressure)
Customer drivers (recurring themes):
- EU-only processing requirements (payments + healthcare + regulated SaaS)
- Procurement checklists now frequently require:
  - “Customer data processed only in selected regions”
  - “Regional failover behavior described and controllable”
  - “Audit logs and evidence of enforcement”

Pipeline impact (not exhaustive; representative):
- Nordholm Payments (EU-only): security review asked for deterministic enforcement and auditable config changes; risk of POC stall without it
- Helix Health Systems: comparing Hosted vs Dedicated; Hosted needs pinning + clear exclusion list for logs/traces
- DACH enterprise prospects: legal/procurement language increasingly expects region controls and incident communication clarity

4) Positioning and messaging
Audience: Engineering leaders, security/compliance teams, platform teams; buyers who value clear guarantees and operational tooling.

Primary message:
“Redwood Hosted now supports region pinning with enforcement. You choose where your content is processed, and Redwood will block requests that would violate your policy—no silent cross-region failover.”

Supporting messages:
- Deterministic controls: enforcement happens at request time; no best-effort routing
- Operational clarity: actionable errors + dashboards + audit logs
- Production-ready: no surprise fallback; explicit configuration and behavior

Proof points to include:
- Error contract examples (consistent code/status + request_id)
- Audit log events for policy changes (who/when/what)
- Dashboard screenshots: blocked requests, cross-region attempt counters, policy eval latency

Non-claims / careful language:
- Do not claim “all customer data stays in region” without the defined scope statement
- Do not imply we replicate data across regions; we enforce processing location for requests and related in-scope telemetry

Suggested external phrasing for security questionnaires:
“Customer content (request/response payloads) is processed only within the configured allowed region set for Hosted API requests. If capacity constraints or fallback would require leaving the allowed set, the request is blocked with a policy violation error. Configuration changes are logged and auditable.”

5) Target customers and rollout cohorts
Primary target segments:
- Regulated payments / fintech
- Healthcare / life sciences
- Enterprise SaaS with EU/UK residency requirements
- Platform teams consolidating inference providers and needing compliance guardrails

Initial target accounts (seed list; expand weekly):
- Nordholm Payments (HubSpot record)
- Helix Health Systems (HubSpot record)
- Active EU-only POC prospects from Feb security review + scoping calls (see Fireflies transcripts)
- Existing enterprise customers who requested EU-only routing controls (via CSM + support tags)

Rollout cohorts:
- Cohort 0: internal dogfood + Redwood staging verification (SRE + Eng + Support)
- Cohort 1: allowlisted enterprise POCs (EU-only)
- Cohort 2: broader enterprise opt-in (Hosted), default-off
- Cohort 3: self-serve opt-in for eligible plans (subject to Product decision; see open questions)

Eligibility constraints (draft):
- Available only in regions where we can provide stable capacity + compliance coverage
- Some models may not be available in all regions at launch; messaging must direct customers to region-available model list

6) Packaging and pricing
Current assumption (needs Product/RevOps confirmation):
- Region pinning enforcement: Enterprise feature (Hosted) included in security/compliance bundle for enterprise plans
- No new line-item pricing for v1; may influence plan tier and SLA packaging

Notes:
- If we decide to expose API-key-level pinning, confirm whether that is limited to enterprise or generally available

7) Launch plan and timeline (draft)
Engineering milestones (informational; dates subject to change):
- Feature flag readiness + end-to-end tests gating: by end of Phase 2
- Console settings + audit log events: in Phase 2–3
- Docs + error code references: before Cohort 1

Go-to-market timeline:
Week 0 (pre-launch):
- Internal enablement session (Sales/SE/Support/CS): 45 mins + Q&A
- Finalize FAQ + security narrative + evidence pack outline
- Publish internal “how to request allowlist + configuration checklist”

Week 1 (Cohort 1):
- Proactive outreach to targeted POCs (Avery/Hannah + SE)
- Offer guided setup (SE-led) and share troubleshooting guide

Week 2–4 (Cohort 2):
- Expand allowlist; begin collecting benchmark data (block-rate, policy evaluation latency, customer satisfaction)
- Iterate on Console troubleshooting UX copy based on support feedback

GA trigger criteria (proposal):
- <0.5% false positive blocks for allowlisted customers over 7 days (excluding customer misconfig)
- No P0/P1 incidents attributable to enforcement for 14 days
- Support macros + runbooks finalized; on-call trained

8) Comms plan
External comms (targeted, not broad blast for initial launch):
- Direct 1:1 email to security contacts + technical owner for Cohort 1/2 accounts
- Optional: short blog/docs announcement after GA (Product/Marketing decision)
- Updated security FAQ + documentation pages as the primary “source of truth” (avoid slideware drifting)

Internal comms:
- #sales, #solutions-engineering, #support, #customer-success announcement with:
  - How to pitch
  - Eligibility + how to request allowlist
  - Known limitations
  - Escalation path for issues

Customer email template (outline):
Subject: Redwood Hosted now supports EU-only processing via Region Pinning (enforced)
Body:
- What changed (you can pin allowed regions; enforcement blocks violations)
- What you need to do (set policy in Console or via admin API)
- What to expect (no cross-region fallback; possible policy blocks if config/region/model mismatch)
- Links: docs, FAQ, troubleshooting, support contact

9) Enablement assets checklist
Sales/SE enablement:
- One-pager: “Hosted Data Residency Enforcement” (what it is / what it isn’t)
- Talk track + objections handling
- Competitive notes (high level): deterministic enforcement + audit logs vs “best effort routing” alternatives

Security/compliance enablement:
- Security FAQ updates (customer-facing)
- Evidence pack (internal) with:
  - Control descriptions
  - Dashboard screenshots
  - Audit log samples
  - Test evidence references

Support enablement:
- Macros for common scenarios:
  - “Your request was blocked because the allowed region set doesn’t include the region your key/project is using”
  - “Model not available in your pinned region”
  - “Streaming endpoint returning unexpected error: collect request_id and timestamp”
- Runbook: residency enforcement false positives (triage, feature-flag override process, comms)

Docs:
- Public docs page: configuration + examples + troubleshooting
- Error codes reference (include request_id, how to contact support)

10) Risks and mitigations
Risk: False positives blocking legitimate traffic (routing/policy bugs)
- Impact: immediate customer-visible outage / POC failure
- Mitigation:
  - Strong E2E test coverage (pinned EU org hitting US endpoint, streaming/non-streaming)
  - Progressive rollout + allowlist
  - Feature flag + quick rollback path
  - SRE alerting on spike in policy blocks

Risk: Support load increases due to misconfiguration
- Impact: higher ticket volume, slower POC cycles
- Mitigation:
  - Console UX that surfaces “why blocked” + “how to fix”
  - Clear docs with common patterns (org vs project vs key precedence)
  - Support macros + short troubleshooting decision tree

Risk: Confusing or inconsistent error messaging (esp. streaming)
- Impact: customers see generic 500s; loss of trust
- Mitigation:
  - Gateway standardization across streaming/non-streaming
  - SDK mapping to typed exception (where applicable)
  - Automated tests for streaming error payload consistency

Risk: Overpromising residency scope (legal/security expectation mismatch)
- Impact: procurement escalation; security review failure
- Mitigation:
  - Tight, reviewed language for “in-scope systems”
  - Explicit exclusions list in FAQ (what’s pinned, what’s not)
  - Security sign-off on outbound copy

Risk: Model availability gaps by region
- Impact: customers pin EU-only but expect model X that is US-only
- Mitigation:
  - Publish per-region model availability list
  - Provide recommended equivalents by region
  - Improve error guidance to point to model availability doc

11) Success metrics (first 30–60 days)
Revenue / pipeline:
- # of POCs unblocked due to residency enforcement
- Conversion rate uplift for regulated EU prospects in pipeline
- # of security reviews where residency is marked “satisfied” without custom exception

Product reliability:
- Blocked request rate by cohort (split: valid enforcement vs false positive)
- Policy evaluation latency (p95/p99)
- Incidents attributed to enforcement (count/severity)

Enablement:
- Support ticket volume tagged “residency pinning” and time-to-resolution
- Docs page engagement + helpfulness feedback from SEs

12) Operational readiness and escalation
Primary escalation (customer-facing issues):
- SE on the account (Markus Klein’s team) + on-call Support lead
- Engineering on-call (SRE) for suspected false positives

What Support/SE should always capture on escalation:
- request_id
- timestamp + region
- org/project identifier
- whether streaming
- pinned policy settings (allowed regions + primary)
- model + endpoint

13) Open questions / decisions needed
(Owners in parentheses)
- Is Region Pinning enforcement enterprise-only at GA, or opt-in for lower tiers? (Naomi + RevOps)
- Do we expose policy_id in the public error response, or only in internal logs/console? (Naomi + Marcus + Brian)
- Default behavior for existing customers: no policy (status quo) vs prompt to configure? (Naomi)
- Dedicated alignment statement: what exactly do we claim as “aligned behavior” in Dedicated? (Markus + Naomi)
- Final GA criteria thresholds (block-rate, incident-free window) and who signs off (Rafael + Priya)

14) Approvals required before Cohort 1
- Product: Naomi Feldman
- Security: Marcus Lin / Dr. Aisha Rahman
- SRE readiness: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Docs readiness: Elliot Price
- Sales enablement readiness: Markus Klein

Appendix A — Suggested talk track (SE/Sales)
“If you need EU-only processing on Hosted, Redwood now lets you pin your project/org to EU regions. The platform enforces this at request time: we won’t silently fail over to the US. If a request can’t be served within EU due to capacity or configuration, you’ll get a deterministic policy violation error with guidance. You also get audit logs for policy changes and dashboards to monitor any blocked requests.”

Appendix B — Common objections and responses (draft)
Q: “Do you replicate our data across regions?”
A: “Not as part of this feature. This is about request processing and enforced routing boundaries. We’ll share the scope statement and what systems are in/out of scope.”

Q: “What happens during an EU capacity event?”
A: “With pinning enabled, we will not cross-region fail over by default. Instead, requests that cannot be served in-region will be blocked with a clear error so you can handle it deterministically (retry/backoff/fallback on your side).”

Q: “Can we pin by API key?”
A: “Optional; depends on the final GA packaging. We can support per-project pinning at minimum and can discuss key-level controls for complex orgs.”
